interpreter: python 3.12.16 (atlas-aci-dev-s16, docker only); tree-sitter-language-pack 1.6.0 / tree-sitter 0.25.2 (equal to uv.lock). The host has no tree-sitter, and no project code runs on the host, so the host half of (a) is not applicable: the pinned grammar is exercised in the dev image only.

notes: class fields: name (constant | scope_resolution for compact `Blog::Tag`), superclass (a `superclass` node whose first named child is the base: constant, or scope_resolution for `::ActiveRecord::Base`; `ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1]` is element_reference(object: scope_resolution, float), `ActiveRecord::Migration` is scope_resolution), body (body_statement); an empty class has NO body field

association call: method (identifier), arguments (argument_list; positional simple_symbol/string/identifier/lambda/splat_argument, pair children), block (do_block); `has_many(*SHARED)` -> splat_argument; `-> { }` -> lambda with a block body
pair: key (hash_key_symbol for `name:`; string for `"name":` and for rocket pairs), value; the `=>` token is a direct child only of rocket pairs
simple_symbol text includes the leading `:`; `:"x"` is delimited_symbol; string with interpolation has an `interpolation` child; a lone `#{` in single quotes stays string_content

table statement: assignment(left: call(receiver: self, method: identifier table_name), right: string | simple_symbol | other); operator_assignment has the same left; `def self.table_name` is singleton_method(object: self, name: identifier)
migration: class body `method` nodes (name identifier, body body_statement; an empty def has no body); `def self.up` is singleton_method; create_table block is do_block under the `block` field
if-modifier statements are if_modifier; bare `reversible` style statements are call with a block

f_rails_fidelity.source: activerecord/lib/active_record/inheritance.rb, ActiveRecord::Inheritance::ClassMethods#compute_type, fetched from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rails/rails/<tag>/ for v7.1.3 (line 240), v7.2.0 (242) and v8.0.0 (242)
f_rails_fidelity.finding: `::`-prefixed names are constantized absolutely; otherwise the candidate list is built by `name.scan(/::|$/) { candidates.unshift "#{$`}::#{type_name}" }` then `candidates << type_name`, and the first candidate whose safe_constantize equals the candidate string wins (deepest first, bare name last). Equal to D5's candidate list; docs claim only the list, not precedence.
